resolve any versions for {req}\")\n\n            # Return first result for backward compatibility\n            return results[0]\n        except Exception as err:\n            if self.multiple_versions:\n                self._record_failed_version(req, \"unresolved\", err, \"failed to resolve\")\n                if self.test_mode:\n                    self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, \"resolution\")\n                return None\n            if not self.test_mode:\n                raise\n            self.record_test_mode_failure(req, None, err, \"resolution\")\n            return None\n\n    def resolve_versions(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        parent_req: Requirement | None = None,\n        return_all_versions: bool = False,\n    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:\n        \"\"\"Resolve version(s) of a requirement.\n\n        Returns list of (source URL, version) tuples, sorted by version (highest first).\n\n        Git URL resolution stays in Bootstrapper because it requires\n        build orchestration (BuildEnvironment, build dependencies).\n        Delegates PyPI/graph resolution to BootstrapRequirementResolver.\n\n        Args:\n            req: Package requirement to resolve\n            req_type: Type of requirement\n            parent_req: Explicit parent requirement from dependency chain.\n                Callers must pass this explicitly; do not read ``self.why`` here.\n            return_all_versions: If True, return all matching versions.\n                If False, return only highest version.\n\n        Returns:\n            List of (url, version) tuples. Contains one item when\n            return_all_versions=False, or all matching versions when True.\n        \"\"\"\n        if req.url:\n            if req_type != RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL:\n                raise ValueError(\n                    f\"{req} includes a URL, but is not a top-level dependency\"\n                )\n\n            # Check cache first to avoid re-resolving\n            # Git URLs are always source (not prebuilt)\n            cached_result = self._resolver.get_matching_versions(req, pre_built=False)\n            if cached_result:\n                logger.debug(f\"resolved {req} from cache\")\n                return cached_result if return_all_versions else [cached_result[0]]\n\n            logger.info(\"resolving source via URL, ignoring any plugins\")\n            source_url, resolved_version = self._resolve_version_from_git_url(req=req)\n            # Cache the git URL resolution (always source, not prebuilt)\n            # Store as list for consistency with cache structure\n            result = [(source_url, resolved_version)]\n            self._resolver.extend_known_versions(req, pre_built=False, result=result)\n            return result  # Git URLs always return single version\n\n        # Delegate to RequirementResolver\n        return self._resolver.resolve(\n            req=req,\n            req_type=req_type,\n            parent_req=parent_req,\n            return_all_versions=return_all_versions,\n        )\n\n    def bootstrap(self, requirements: list[Requirement]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Bootstrap all top-level requirements and their transitive dependencies.\n\n        .. versionadded:: 0.89\n           Replaces the former ``bootstrap(req, req_type)`` signature.\n\n        Resolves each requirement, adds it to the dependency graph, and processes\n        the full dependency tree using an iterative DFS loop. Handles\n        ``requirement_ctxvar`` context internally; callers do not need to manage it.\n\n        In test mode, records failures and continues instead of raising. In\n        ``multiple_versions`` mode, processes all matching versions per requirement.\n\n        Args:\n            requirements: Top-level requirements to resolve and bootstrap.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Resolve all top-level reqs and build initial stack.\n        # Use the token pattern (no try/finally) so that if resolution raises\n        # in normal mode, the context var stays set for the top-level error\n        # handler in __main__.py to include the package name in its log message.\n        stack: list[Phase] = []\n        initial_items: list[Phase] = []\n        for req in requirements:\n            token = requirement_ctxvar.set(req)\n            result = self._resolve_and_add_top_level(req)\n            requirement_ctxvar.reset(token)\n            if result is not None:\n                initial_items.append(\n                    Resolve(\n                        WorkItem(\n                            req=req,\n                            req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,\n                            why_snapshot=[],\n                            parent=None,\n                        )\n                    )\n                )\n        self._push_items(stack, initial_items)\n\n        self._run_bootstrap_loop(stack)\n\n    def _run_bootstrap_loop(self, stack: list[Phase]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Run the iterative DFS bootstrap loop over a pre-built work stack.\n\n        Pops items one at a time, dispatches each phase, and pushes any\n        follow-on items (continuations and new dependencies) back onto the\n        stack. Updates the progress bar as items complete.\n\n        Args:\n            stack: Initial list of ``Phase`` objects to process. Modified\n                in-place; empty on return.\n        \"\"\"\n        while stack:\n            self._record_stack_state(stack)\n            item = stack.pop()\n            self.why = list(item.work_item.why_snapshot)\n\n            with (\n                req_ctxvar_context(item.work_item.req, item.work_item.resolved_version),\n                self._track_why(item),\n            ):\n                if item.requires_exclusive_run:\n                    logger.info(\n                        \"%s requires exclusive build, draining background pool\",\n                        item.work_item.req,\n                    )\n                    self._drain_background_pool()\n                try:\n                    new_items = item.run(self)\n                except Exception as err:\n                    new_items = self._handle_phase_error(item, err)\n\n            new_dep_count = sum(1 for it in new_items if isinstance(it, Resolve))\n            if new_dep_count > 0:\n                self.progressbar.update_total(new_dep_count)\n            if not new_items:\n                self.progressbar.update()\n\n            self._push_items(stack, new_items)\n\n    def _bootstrap_one(self, req: Requirement, req_type: RequirementType) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Bootstrap a single requirement using an iterative DFS loop.\n\n        Internal method used only by the git URL resolution path\n        (``_handle_build_requirements``). All other callers should use\n        ``bootstrap(requirements)`` instead.\n\n        Uses an explicit LIFO stack instead of recursion to handle arbitrarily\n        deep dependency graphs without hitting Python's recursion limit.\n\n        In test mode, catches build exceptions, records package name, and continues.\n        In normal mode, raises exceptions immediately (fail-fast).\n\n        When multiple_versions is enabled, bootstraps all matching versions instead\n        of just the highest version.\n        \"\"\"\n        logger.info(f\"bootstrapping {req} as {req_type} dependency of {self.why[-1:]}\")\n\n        # Capture parent from current why stack before creating work items\n        parent: tuple[Requirement, Version] | None = None\n        if self.why:\n            _, parent_req, parent_version = self.why[-1]\n            parent = (parent_req, parent_version)\n\n        # Save the why stack so we can restore it after the iterative loop\n        # (the loop modifies self.why for each work item)\n        saved_why = list(self.why)\n\n        # Single RESOLVE item — resolution, version expansion, and error\n        # handling all happen inside the loop via Resolve.run().\n        initial_item = Resolve(\n            WorkItem(\n                req=req,\n                req_type=req_type,\n                why_snapshot=list(self.why),\n                parent=parent,\n            )\n        )\n        stack: list[Phase] = []\n        self._push_items(stack, [initial_item])\n\n        self._run_bootstrap_loop(stack)\n\n        # empty the stack state file to show watchers are are done\n        # with bootstrapping\n        self._record_stack_state([])\n\n        # Restore why stack for the caller\n        self.why = saved_why\n\n    @contextlib.contextmanager\n    def _track_why(\n        self,\n        item: Phase,\n    ) -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:\n        \"\"\"Context manager to track dependency chain in self.why stack.\n\n        No-op for phases where tracks_why is False (RESOLVE and START).\n        For all other phases, pushes the item onto the why stack and\n        ensures it is popped even if an exception occurs.\n        \"\"\"\n        if not item.tracks_why:\n            yield\n            return\n        wi = item.work_item\n        assert wi.resolved_version is not None\n        self.why.append((wi.req_type, wi.req, wi.resolved_version))\n        try:\n            yield\n        finally:\n            self.why.pop()\n\n    def record_test_mode_failure(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        version: str | None,\n        err: Exception,\n        failure_type: FailureType,\n        log_level: typing.Literal[\"error\", \"warning\"] = \"error\",\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Record a failure in test mode. Call this after checking test_mode.\n\n        Args:\n            req: The requirement that failed.\n            version: The version being processed (None if not yet resolved).\n            err: The exception that was raised.\n            failure_type: Category of failure for analysis.\n            log_level: Log at error (fatal) or warning (non-fatal, continuing).\n        \"\"\"\n        version_str = f\"=={version}\" if version else \"\"\n        msg = f\"test mode: {failure_type} failed for {req.name}{version_str}\"\n        if log_level == \"warning\":\n            logger.warning(\"%s: %s (continuing)\", msg, err)\n        else:\n            logger.error(\"%s: %s\", msg, err, exc_info=True)\n\n        self.failed_packages.append(\n            {\n                \"package\": str(req.name),\n                \"version\": version,\n                \"exception_type\": err.__class__.__name__,\n                \"exception_message\": str(err),\n                \"failure_type\": failure_type,\n            }\n        )\n\n    @property\n    def explain(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Return message formatting current version of why stack.\"\"\"\n        return \" for \".join(\n            f\"{req_type} dependency {req} ({resolved_version})\"\n            for req_type, req, resolved_version in reversed(self.why)\n        )\n\n    def _prepare_build_dependencies(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        resolved_version: Version | None,\n        sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path,\n        build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment,\n    ) -> set[Requirement]:\n        \"\"\"Prepare build dependencies for a package.\n\n        Only used by the git URL resolution path\n        (_resolve_version_from_git_url -> _get_version_from_package_metadata).\n        The main iterative bootstrap loop handles build deps via phase handlers.\n        \"\"\"\n        # build system\n        build_system_dependencies = dependencies.get_build_system_dependencies(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            req=req,\n            version=resolved_version,\n            sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,\n        )\n        self._handle_build_requirements(\n            req,\n            RequirementType.BUILD_SYSTEM,\n            build_system_dependencies,\n        )\n        # The next hooks need build system requirements.\n        build_env.install(build_system_dependencies)\n\n        # build backend\n        build_backend_dependencies = dependencies.get_build_backend_dependencies(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            req=req,\n            version=resolved_version,\n            sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,\n            build_env=build_env,\n        )\n\n        # build sdist\n        build_sdist_dependencies = dependencies.get_build_sdist_dependencies(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            req=req,\n            version=resolved_version,\n            sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,\n            build_env=build_env,\n        )\n\n        # Filter out deps already satisfied by build-system dependencies\n        resolved_build_sys = self._resolve_build_system_versions_by_name(\n            build_system_dependencies,\n        )\n        build_backend_dependencies = self.filter_deps_satisfied_by_build_system(\n            build_backend_dependencies,\n            resolved_build_sys,\n            RequirementType.BUILD_BACKEND,\n        )\n        build_sdist_dependencies = self.filter_deps_satisfied_by_build_system(\n            build_sdist_dependencies,\n            resolved_build_sys,\n            RequirementType.BUILD_SDIST,\n        )\n\n        self._handle_build_requirements(\n            req,\n            RequirementType.BUILD_BACKEND,\n            build_backend_dependencies,\n        )\n        self._handle_build_requirements(\n            req,\n            RequirementType.BUILD_SDIST,\n            build_sdist_dependencies,\n        )\n\n        build_dependencies = build_sdist_dependencies | build_backend_dependencies\n        if build_dependencies.isdisjoint(build_system_dependencies):\n            build_env.install(build_dependencies)\n\n        return (\n            build_system_dependencies\n            | build_backend_dependencies\n            | build_sdist_dependencies\n        )\n\n    def _handle_build_requirements(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        build_type: RequirementType,\n        build_dependencies: set[Requirement],\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Bootstrap build dependencies.\n\n        Only used by the git URL resolution path\n        (_resolve_version_from_git_url -> _get_version_from_package_metadata).\n        The main iterative bootstrap loop handles build deps via phase handlers.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.progressbar.update_total(len(build_dependencies))\n\n        for dep in self._sort_requirements(build_dependencies):\n            with req_ctxvar_context(dep):\n                # Save/restore self.why because the iterative bootstrap()\n                # modifies it internally for each work item.\n                saved_why = list(self.why)\n                self._bootstrap_one(req=dep, req_type=build_type)\n                self.why = saved_why\n            self.progressbar.update()\n\n    def _download_prebuilt(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        resolved_version: Version,\n        wheel_url: str,\n    ) -> tuple[pathlib.Path, pathlib.Path]:\n        result = _cache._bg_prepare_prebuilt(\n            self.ctx, req, req_type, resolved_version, wheel_url\n        )\n        assert result.wheel_filename is not None\n        assert result.unpack_dir is not None\n        return (result.wheel_filename, result.unpack_dir)\n\n    def _download_source(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        resolved_version: Version,\n        source_url: str,\n    ) -> pathlib.Path:\n        \"\"\"Download source for a package.\"\"\"\n        result: pathlib.Path = sources.download_source(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            req=req,\n            version=resolved_version,\n            download_url=source_url,\n        )\n        return result\n\n    def _prepare_source(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        resolved_version: Version,\n        source_filename: pathlib.Path,\n    ) -> pathlib.Path:\n        \"\"\"Prepare (unpack/patch) source for building.\"\"\"\n        result: pathlib.Path = sources.prepare_source(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            req=req,\n            source_filename=source_filename,\n            version=resolved_version,\n        )\n        return result\n\n    def _handle_test_mode_failure(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        resolved_version: Version,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        build_error: Exception,\n    ) -> SourceBuildResult | None:\n        \"\"\"Handle build failure in test mode by attempting pre-built fallback.\n\n        Args:\n            req: The requirement that failed to build.\n            resolved_version: The version that was attempted.\n            req_type: The type of requirement (for fallback resolution).\n            build_error: The original exception from the build attempt.\n\n        Returns:\n            SourceBuildResult if fallback succeeded, None if fallback also failed.\n        \"\"\"\n        logger.warning(\n            \"test mode: build failed for %s==%s, attempting pre-built fallback: %s\",\n            req.name,\n            resolved_version,\n            build_error,\n        )\n\n        try:\n            parent_req = self.why[-1][1] if self.why else None\n            results = self._resolver.resolve(\n                req=req,\n                req_type=req_type,\n                parent_req=parent_req,\n                pre_built=True,  # Force prebuilt for test mode fallback\n            )\n            wheel_url, fallback_version = results[0]\n\n            if fallback_version != resolved_version:\n                logger.warning(\n                    \"test mode: version mismatch for %s - requested %s, fallback %s\",\n                    req.name,\n                    resolved_version,\n                    fallback_version,\n                )\n\n            wheel_filename, unpack_dir = self._download_prebuilt(\n                req=req,\n                req_type=req_type,\n                resolved_version=fallback_version,\n                wheel_url=wheel_url,\n            )\n\n            logger.info(\n                \"test mode: successfully used pre-built wheel for %s==%s\",\n                req.name,\n                fallback_version,\n            )\n\n            # Package succeeded via fallback - no failure to record\n\n            return SourceBuildResult(\n                wheel_filename=wheel_filename,\n                sdist_filename=None,\n                unpack_dir=unpack_dir,\n                sdist_root_dir=None,\n                build_env=None,\n                source_type=SourceType.PREBUILT,\n            )\n\n        except Exception as fallback_error:\n            logger.error(\n                \"test mode: pre-built fallback also failed for %s: %s\",\n                req.name,\n                fallback_error,\n                exc_info=True,\n            )\n            # Return None to signal failure; bootstrap() will record via re-raised exception\n            return None\n\n    def _resolve_version_from_git_url(self, req: Requirement) -> tuple[str, Version]:\n        \"\"\"Resolve source path and version from a ``git+`` URL.\n\n        Parses the URL for an ``@ref`` version hint. If the ref is a valid\n        version, reuses an existing clone when possible. Otherwise, clones\n        the repo and extracts the version from package metadata.\n        \"\"\"\n\n        if not req.url:\n            raise ValueError(f\"unable to resolve from URL with no URL in {req}\")\n\n        # We start by not knowing where we would put the source because we don't\n        # know the version.\n        working_src_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None\n        version: Version | None = None\n\n        url_to_clone, git_ref = gitutils.parse_vcs_url(req.url, require_ref=False)\n        need_to_clone = False\n\n        if git_ref == gitutils.GIT_HEAD:\n            # No ref in URL, clone to discover the version.\n            logger.debug(\"no reference in URL, will clone\")\n            need_to_clone = True\n        else:\n            # If we have a reference, it might be a valid python version\n            # string, or not. It _must_ be a valid git reference. If it can\n            # be parsed as a valid python version, we assume the tag points\n            # to source that will think that is its version, so we allow\n            # reusing an existing cloned repo if there is one.\n            try:\n                version = Version(git_ref)\n            except ValueError:\n                logger.info(\n                    \"could not parse %r as a version, cloning to get the version\",\n                    git_ref,\n                )\n                need_to_clone = True\n            else:\n                logger.info(\"URL %s includes version %s\", req.url, version)\n                working_src_dir = (\n                    self.ctx.work_dir\n                    / f\"{req.name}-{version}\"\n                    / f\"{req.name}-{version}\"\n                )\n                if not working_src_dir.exists():\n                    need_to_clone = True\n                else:\n                    if self.ctx.cleanup:\n                        logger.debug(\"cleaning up %s to reclone\", working_src_dir)\n                        shutil.rmtree(working_src_dir)\n                        need_to_clone = True\n                    else:\n                        logger.info(\"reusing %s\", working_src_dir)\n\n        if need_to_clone:\n            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:\n                clone_dir = pathlib.Path(tmpdir) / \"src\"\n                sources.download_git_source(\n                    ctx=self.ctx,\n                    req=req,\n                    url_to_clone=url_to_clone,\n                    destination_dir=clone_dir,\n                    ref=git_ref,\n                )\n                if not version:\n                    # If we still do not have a version, get it from the package\n                    # metadata.\n                    version = self._get_version_from_package_metadata(req, clone_dir)\n                    logger.info(\"found version %s\", version)\n                    working_src_dir = (\n                        self.ctx.work_dir\n                        / f\"{req.name}-{version}\"\n                        / f\"{req.name}-{version}\"\n                    )\n                    if working_src_dir.exists():\n                        # We have to check if the destination directory exists\n                        # because if we were not given a version we did not\n                        # clean it up earlier. We do not use ctx.cleanup to\n                        # control this action because we cannot trust that the\n                        # destination directory is reusable because we have had\n                        # to compute the version and we cannot be sure that the\n                        # version is dynamic. Two different commits in the repo\n                        # could have the same version if that version is set\n                        # with static data in the repo instead of via a tag or\n                        # dynamically computed by something like setuptools-scm.\n                        logger.debug(\"cleaning up %s\", working_src_dir)\n                        shutil.rmtree(working_src_dir)\n                assert working_src_dir is not None\n                working_src_dir.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n                logger.info(\"moving cloned repo to %s\", working_src_dir)\n                shutil.move(clone_dir, str(working_src_dir))\n\n        if not version:\n            raise ValueError(f\"unable to determine version for {req}\")\n\n        if not working_src_dir:\n            raise ValueError(f\"unable to determine working source directory for {req}\")\n\n        logging.info(\"resolved from git URL to %s, %s\", working_src_dir, version)\n        return (str(working_src_dir), version)\n\n    def _get_version_from_package_metadata(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        source_dir: pathlib.Path,\n    ) -> Version:\n        pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)\n        build_dir = pbi.build_dir(source_dir)\n\n        logger.info(\n            \"preparing build dependencies so we can access the metadata to get the version\"\n        )\n        build_env = build_environment.BuildEnvironment(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            parent_dir=source_dir.parent,\n        )\n        build_dependencies = self._prepare_build_dependencies(\n            req=req,\n            resolved_version=None,\n            sdist_root_dir=source_dir,\n            build_env=build_env,\n        )\n        build_env.install(build_dependencies)\n\n        logger.info(\"generating metadata to get version\")\n        hook_caller = dependencies.get_build_backend_hook_caller(\n            ctx=self.ctx,\n            req=req,\n            build_dir=build_dir,\n            override_environ={},\n            build_env=build_env,\n        )\n        metadata_dir_base = hook_caller.prepare_metadata_for_build_wheel(\n            metadata_directory=str(source_dir.parent),\n            config_settings=pbi.config_settings,\n        )\n        metadata_filename = source_dir.parent / metadata_dir_base / \"METADATA\"\n        # Disable validation because some packages have metadata version mismatches\n        # (e.g., declaring Metadata-Version: 2.2 but using fields from 2.4).\n        metadata = dependencies.parse_metadata(metadata_filename, validate=False)\n        return metadata.version\n\n    def add_to_graph(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        req_version: Version,\n        download_url: str,\n        parent: tuple[Requirement, Version] | None,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Add a resolved requirement as a node/edge in the dependency graph.\n\n        Records the dependency relationship between ``parent`` and ``req`` in\n        the in-memory graph, then writes the updated graph to disk. Must be\n        called after resolution but before the seen-check so that every edge\n        is captured even for packages that are not built again.\n\n        Args:\n            req: The requirement being added.\n            req_type: Whether this is a build-system, build-backend, install,\n                or other dependency kind.\n            req_version: The resolved version of ``req``.\n            download_url: Source URL used to obtain the distribution.\n            parent: ``(req, version)`` of the package that introduced ``req``,\n                or ``None`` for top-level requirements.\n        \"\"\"\n        parent_req, parent_version = parent if parent else (None, None)\n        pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)\n        # Update the dependency graph after we determine that this requirement is\n        # useful but before we determine if it is redundant so that we capture all\n        # edges to use for building a valid constraints file.\n        self.ctx.dependency_graph.add_dependency(\n            parent_name=canonicalize_name(parent_req.name) if parent_req else None,\n            parent_version=parent_version,\n            req_type=req_type,\n            req=req,\n            req_version=req_version,\n            download_url=download_url,\n            pre_built=pbi.pre_built,\n            constraint=self.ctx.constraints.get_constraint(req.name),\n        )\n        self.ctx.write_to_graph_to_file()\n\n    def _sort_requirements(\n        self,\n        requirements: typing.Iterable[Requirement],\n    ) -> typing.Iterable[Requirement]:\n        return sorted(requirements, key=operator.attrgetter(\"name\"))\n\n    def _resolved_key(\n        self, req: Requirement, version: Version, typ: typing.Literal[\"sdist\", \"wheel\"]\n    ) -> SeenKey:\n        return (\n            canonicalize_name(req.name),\n            tuple(sorted(req.extras)),\n            str(version),\n            typ,\n        )\n\n    def mark_as_seen(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        version: Version,\n        sdist_only: bool = False,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Track sdist and wheel builds\n\n        A sdist-only build just contains as an sdist.\n        A wheel build counts as wheel and sdist, because the presence of a\n        either implies we have built a wheel from an sdist or we have a\n        prebuilt wheel that will never have an sdist.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Mark sdist seen for sdist-only build and wheel build\n        self._seen_requirements.add(self._resolved_key(req, version, \"sdist\"))\n        if not sdist_only:\n            # Mark wheel seen only for wheel build\n            self._seen_requirements.add(self._resolved_key(req, version, \"wheel\"))\n\n    def has_been_seen(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        version: Version,\n        sdist_only: bool = False,\n    ) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Return True if this requirement/version has already been processed.\n\n        Uses the same sdist-vs-wheel distinction as ``mark_as_seen``:\n        when ``sdist_only`` is True, checks only for a prior sdist build;\n        otherwise checks for a prior wheel build.\n\n        Args:\n            req: The requirement to check.\n            version: The resolved version to check.\n            sdist_only: If True, check for a sdist-only build instead of a\n                full wheel build.\n        \"\"\"\n        typ: typing.Literal[\"sdist\", \"wheel\"] = \"sdist\" if sdist_only else \"wheel\"\n        return self._resolved_key(req, version, typ) in self._seen_requirements\n\n    def add_to_build_order(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        version: Version,\n        source_url: str,\n        source_type: SourceType,\n        prebuilt: bool = False,\n        constraint: Requirement | None = None,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Append a package to the build-order output file if not already present.\n\n        Deduplicates by ``(canonicalized_name, version)`` so the same package\n        is never written twice, regardless of extras. On each new entry, the\n        full build-order list is written to ``self._build_order_filename``.\n\n        Args:\n            req: The requirement being added to the build order.\n            version: The resolved version.\n            source_url: URL from which the source distribution was obtained.\n            source_type: The kind of source (sdist, wheel, git, etc.).\n            prebuilt: True if the wheel was taken from a prebuilt cache rather\n                than compiled locally.\n            constraint: The version constraint active for this package, if any.\n        \"\"\"\n        # We only care if this version of this package has been built,\n        # and don't want to trigger building it twice.        for dep in self._sort_requirements(deps)\n        ]\n\n    def _resolve_build_system_versions_by_name(\n        self,\n        build_system_deps: set[Requirement],\n    ) -> dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]]:\n        \"\"\"Build a mapping of resolved build-system versions by looking up graph nodes.\n\n        Used by the git URL path where the parent node may not yet exist\n        in the dependency graph.\n        \"\"\"\n        resolved: dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]] = {}\n        for dep in build_system_deps:\n            dep_name = canonicalize_name(dep.name)\n            nodes = self.ctx.dependency_graph.get_nodes_by_name(str(dep_name))\n            for node in nodes:\n                if node.version in dep.specifier:\n                    resolved[dep_name] = (node.version, node.download_url)\n                    break\n        return resolved\n\n    def get_resolved_build_system_versions(\n        self,\n        item: in the dependency\n        graph to find what versions were resolved for each build-system\n        dependency.\n\n        Returns:\n            Mapping of canonicalized package name to ``(version, download_url)``.\n        \"\"\"\n        assert item.resolved_version is not None\n        parent_key = f\"{canonicalize_name(item.req.name)}=={item.resolved_version}\"\n        parent_node = self.ctx.dependency_graph.nodes.get(parent_key)\n        if parent_node is None:\n            return {}\n        resolved: dict[NormalizedName, tuple[Version, str]] = {}\n        for edge in parent_node.children:\n            if edge.req_type == RequirementType.BUILD_SYSTEM:\n                child = edge.destination_node\n                resolved[child.canonicalized_name] = (\n                    child.version,\n                    child.download_url,\n                )\n        return resolved\n\n    def filter_deps_satisfied_by_build_system(\n        self,\n        deps: set[Requirement]:\n        \"\"\"Filter out deps already satisfied by build-system dependencies.\n\n        For each dep whose resolved build-system version satisfies the\n        requirement specifier, excludes the dep from the returned set.\n        When *parent* is provided, also adds a graph edge reusing that\n        version.  Remaining deps need independent resolution.\n\n        Logs a warning when the same package appears in both build-system\n        and build-backend/sdist with incompatible version specifiers.\n        \"\"\"\n        unsatisfied: set[Requirement] = set()\n        for dep in deps:\n            if dep.extras:\n                unsatisfied.add(dep)\n                continue\n            dep_name = canonicalize_name(dep.name)\n            if dep_name in resolved_build_sys:\n                version, download_url = resolved_build_sys[dep_name]\n                if version in dep.specifier:\n                    logger.info(\n                        \"%s dependency %s is already satisfied by \"\n                        \"build-system dependency %s==%s\",\n                        dep_req_type,\n                        dep,\n                        dep_name,\n                        version,\n                    )\n                    if parent is not None:\n                        self.add_to_graph(\n                            req=dep,\n                            req_type=dep_req_type,\n                            req_version=version,\n                            download_url=download_url,\n                            parent=parent,\n                        )\n                    continue\n                else:\n                    logger.warning(\n                        \"%s dependency %s conflicts with \"\n                        \"build-system dependency %s==%s; Multiple versions mode: record failure, remove from graph, continue\n        if self.multiple_versions:\n            assert wi.resolved_version is not None\n            pkg_name = canonicalize_name(wi.req.name)\n            self._record_failed_version(\n                wi.req,\n                str(wi.resolved_version),\n                err,\n                f\"failed during {type(item).phase} phase\",\n            )\n            self.ctx.dependency_graph.remove_dependency(pkg_name, wi.resolved_version)\n            self._seen_requirements.discard(\n                self._resolved_key(wi.req, wi.resolved_version, \"sdist\")\n            )\n            self._seen_requirements.discard(\n                self._resolved_key(wi.req, wi.resolved_version, \"wheel\")\n            )\n            self.ctx.write_to_graph_to_file()\n            return []\n\n        # build_sdist_deps=build_sdist_deps if build_sdist_deps is not None else set(),\n        pbi_pre_built=pbi_pre_built,\n        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,\n        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,\n    )\n    return _PHASE_TO_CLASS[phase](wi)\n\n\nclass TestPhaseClassVariables:\n    \"\"\"Verify class-variable declarations on each Phase subclass.\"\"\"\n\n assert cls.tracks_why == expected_tracks_why\n\n    def test_str_default(self) -> None:\n        wi = _make_work_item(req=\"mypkg\")\n        item = Build(wi)\n        assert str(item) == bt._handle_phase_error(item, err)\n\n\nclass TestIterativeBootstrapLoop:\n    def test_full_lifecycle_source_package(self, tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Drive a package through  original_start_run = Start.run\n\n        def resolve_run(\n            self: Resolve, bt_arg: bootstrapper.Bootstrapper\n        ) -> list[Phase]:\n            phases_visited.append(type(self).phase)\n            return original_resolve_run(self, bt_arg)\n\n        def start_run(self: Start, bt_arg: bootstrapper.Bootstrapper) -> list[Phase]:\n            phases_visited.append(type(self).phase)\n            return original_start_run(self, bt_arg)\n\n        def prepare_source_run(\n            self: PrepareSource, bt_arg: bootstrapper.Bootstrapper\n \"pkg-1.0\" / \"pkg-1.0\"\n            return [PrepareBuild(wi)]\n\n        def prepare_build_run(\n            self: PrepareBuild, bt_arg: bootstrapper.Bootstrapper\n        ) -> list[Phase]:\n phases_visited.append(type(self).phase)\n            wi = self.work_item\n            wi.build_result = SourceBuildResult(\n                wheel_filename=None,\n                sdist_filename=None,\n                unpack_dir=tmp_context.work_dir,\n                sdist_root_dir=None,\n                build_env=None,\n                source_type=SourceType.SDIST,\n            )\n            return [ProcessInstallDeps(wi)]\n\n        def process_install_deps_run(\n            self: ProcessInstallDeps, bt_arg: bootstrapper.Bootstrapper\n        ) -> list[Phase]:\n            phases_visited.append(type(self).phase)\n            return [Complete(self.work_item)]\n\n        def complete_run(\n            self: Complete, bt_arg: bootstrapper.Bootstrapper\n        ) -> list[Phase]:\n            phases_visited.append(type(self).phase)\n            return []\n\n        with (\n            patch.object(Resolve, \"run\", resolve_run),\n            patch.object(Start, \"run\", start_run),\n            patch.object(PrepareSource, \"run\", prepare_source_run),\n            patch.object(PrepareBuild, \"run\", prepare_build_run),\n            patch.object(Build, \"run\", build_run),\n            patch.object(ProcessInstallDeps, \"run\", process_install_deps_run),\n            patch.object(Complete, \"run\", complete_run),\n            patch.object(\n                bt._resolver,\n                \"resolve\",\n                return_value=[(\"https://pypi.org/pkg-1.0.tar.gz\", Version(\"1.0\"))],\n            ),\n        ):\n            bt._bootstrap_one(Requirement(\"pkg\"), RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL)\n\n        assert phases_visited == [\n            BootstrapPhase.RESOLVE,\n            BootstrapPhase.START,\n            BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE,\n            BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_BUILD,\n            BootstrapPhase.BUILD,\n            BootstrapPhase.PROCESS_INSTALL_DEPS,\n            BootstrapPhase.COMPLETE,\n        ]\n\n    def test_lifo_ordering_deps_before_continuation(\n        self, tmp_context: WorkContext\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Verify dependencies are processed before the parent continues.\"\"\"\n        bt = bootstrapper.Bootstrapper(tmp_context)\n\n        processing_order: list[tuple[str, str]] = []\n        original_resolve_run = Resolve.run\n        original_start_run = Start.run\n\n        def resolve_run(\n            self: Resolve, bt_arg: bootstrapper.Bootstrapper\n        ) -> list[Phase]:\n            processing_order.append(\n                (str(self.work_item.req.name), str(type(self).phase))\n            )\n            return original_resolve_run(self, bt_arg)\n\n        def start_run(self: Start, bt_arg: bootstrapper.Bootstrapper) -> list[Phase]:\n            processing_order.append(\n                (str(self.work_item.req.name), str(type(self).phase))\n            )\n            return original_start_run(self, bt_arg)\n\n        def prepare_source_run(\n            self: PrepareSource, bt_arg: bootstrapper.Bootstrapper\n        ) -> list[Phase]:\n            phase_name = str(type(self).phase)\n            req_name = str(self.work_item.req.name)\n            processing_order.append((req_name, phase_name))\n            wi = self.work_item\n            if req_name == \"parent\":\n                assert wi.resolved_version is not None\n                dep_item = Resolve(\n                    WorkItem(\n                        req=Requirement(\"child\"),\n                        req_type=RequirementType.BUILD_SYSTEM,\n                        why_snapshot=[],\n                        parent=(wi.req, wi.resolved_version),\n                    )\n                )\n                return [Complete(wi), dep_item]\n            return []\n\n        def complete_run(\n            self: Complete, bt_arg: bootstrapper.Bootstrapper\n        ) -> list[Phase]:\n            processing_order.append(\n                (str(self.work_item.req.name), str(type(self).phase))\n            )\n            return []\n\n        # Pre-add parent to graph so child can reference it as parent\n        tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(\n            parent_name=None,\n            parent_version=None,\n            req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,\n            req=Requirement(\"parent\"),\n            req_version=Version(\"1.0\"),\n            download_url=\"https://pypi.org/pkg-1.0.tar.gz\",\n            pre_built=False,\n        )\n\n        with (\n child's RESOLVE and START must appear before parent's COMPLETE\n        req_phase_pairs = [\n            (name, phase)\n            for name, phase in processing_order\n            if name in \"complete\"\n        )\n        child_indices = [i for i, (n, _) in enumerate(req_phase_pairs) if n == \"child\"]\n\n        assert all(idx < parent_complete_idx for idx in child_indices), (\n            f\"child must be processed before parent completes: {req_phase_pairs}\"\n        )\n\n    def test_multiple_versions_error_isolation(self, tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Each TestPhaseClassVariables:\n    \"\"\"Verify class-variable declarations on each Phase subclass.\"\"\"\n\n    @pytest.mark.parametrize(\n        \"cls, expected_phase, expected_tracks_why\",\n bt._handle_phase_error(item, err)\n\n\nclass TestIterativeBootstrapLoop:\n    def test_full_lifecycle_source_package(self, tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Drive a package through phases_visited.append(type(self).phase)\n            return original_start_run(self, bt_arg)\n\n        def prepare_source_run(\n            self: PrepareSource, bt_arg: bootstrapper.Bootstrapper\n [ProcessInstallDeps(wi)]\n\n        def process_install_deps_run(\n            self: ProcessInstallDeps, bt_arg: bootstrapper.Bootstrapper\n        ) -> list[Phase]:\n            phases_visited.append(type(self).phase)\n            return [Complete(self.work_item)]\n\n        def complete_run(\n            self: Complete, bt_arg: bootstrapper.Bootstrapper\n        ) -> list[Phase]:\n            phases_visited.append(type(self).phase)\n            return []\n\n        with (\n            patch.object(Resolve, \"run\", resolve_run),\n            patch.object(Start, BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE,\n            BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_BUILD,\n            BootstrapPhase.BUILD,\n            BootstrapPhase.PROCESS_INSTALL_DEPS,\n            BootstrapPhase.COMPLETE,\n        ]\n\n    def test_lifo_ordering_deps_before_continuation(\n        self, tmp_context: WorkContext\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Verify dependencies are processed before the parent (str(self.work_item.req.name), str(type(self).phase))\n            )\n            return original_resolve_run(self, bt_arg)\n\n        def start_run(self: Start, bt_arg: bootstrapper.Bootstrapper) -> def prepare_source_run(\n            self: PrepareSource, bt_arg: bootstrapper.Bootstrapper\n        ) -> list[Phase]:\n            phase_name = str(type(self).phase)\n            req_name = parent\n        tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(\n            parent_name=None,\n            parent_version=None,\n            req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,\n )\n\n    def test_satisfied_dep_reuses_build_system_version(\n        self, tmp_context: WorkContext\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"A build-backend dep with no pin reuses the build-system """Tests for the iterative bootstrap implementation.

Tests cover:
- Phase class hierarchy: class variables and base class behavior
- WorkItem dataclass defaults and state accumulation
- _track_why context manager behavior
- create_unresolved_work_items helper
- Resolve.run() version expansion
- Start.run() graph addition and seen-check
- PrepareSource.run() all branches (prebuilt, source, cached, bad path)
- PrepareBuild.run() dep installation and extraction
- Build.run() conditional install and result construction
- ProcessInstallDeps.run() hooks, dep extraction, error modes
- Complete.run() cleanup
- _handle_phase_error for all three error modes
- End-to-end iterative loop with LIFO ordering
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import concurrent.futures
import pathlib
import typing
from unittest.mock import Mock, call, patch

import pytest
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version
from resolvelib.resolvers import ResolverException

from fromager import bootstrapper, build_environment
from fromager.bootstrapper._build import Build
from fromager.bootstrapper._complete import Complete
from fromager.bootstrapper._phase import Phase
from fromager.bootstrapper._prepare_build import PrepareBuild
from fromager.bootstrapper._prepare_source import PrepareSource
from fromager.bootstrapper._process_install_deps import ProcessInstallDeps
from fromager.bootstrapper._resolve import Resolve
from fromager.bootstrapper._start import Start
from fromager.bootstrapper._types import (
    BootstrapPhase,
    PreparedSourceData,
    SourceBuildResult,
)
from fromager.bootstrapper._work_item import WorkItem
from fromager.context import WorkContext
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType, SourceType


def _make_resolved_future(
    result: typing.Any,
) -> concurrent.futures.Future[typing.Any]:
    """Return an already-completed Future carrying *result*."""
    future: concurrent.futures.Future[typing.Any] = concurrent.futures.Future()
    future.set_result(result)
    return future


def _make_work_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
    source_url: str | None = None,
    version: str | None = None,
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    unpack_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_result: SourceBuildResult | None = None,
    build_system_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_backend_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_sdist_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    pbi_pre_built: bool = False,
    cached_wheel_filename: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_sdist_only: bool = False,
) -> WorkItem:
    return WorkItem(
        req=Requirement(req),
        req_type=req_type,
        why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
        parent=parent,
        source_url=source_url,
        resolved_version=Version(version) if version else None,
        build_env=build_env,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        unpack_dir=unpack_dir,
        build_result=build_result,
        build_system_deps=build_system_deps if build_system_deps is not None else set(),
        build_backend_deps=build_backend_deps
        if build_backend_deps is not None
        else set(),
        build_sdist_deps=build_sdist_deps if build_sdist_deps is not None else set(),
        pbi_pre_built=pbi_pre_built,
        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,
        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,
    )


def _make_resolve_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
) -> Resolve:
    return Resolve(
        WorkItem(
            req=Requirement(req),
            req_type=req_type,
            why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
            parent=parent,
        )
    )


def _make_start_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    source_url: str = "https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.0.tar.gz",
    version: str = "1.0",
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
) -> Start:
    return Start(
        WorkItem(
            req=Requirement(req),
            req_type=req_type,
            why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
            parent=parent,
            source_url=source_url,
            resolved_version=Version(version),
        )
    )


_PHASE_TO_CLASS: dict[BootstrapPhase, type[Phase]] = {
    BootstrapPhase.RESOLVE: Resolve,
    BootstrapPhase.START: Start,
    BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE: PrepareSource,
    BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_BUILD: PrepareBuild,
    BootstrapPhase.BUILD: Build,
    BootstrapPhase.PROCESS_INSTALL_DEPS: ProcessInstallDeps,
    BootstrapPhase.COMPLETE: Complete,
}

    req: str = "testpkg",
    version: str = "1.0",

    unpack_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,

    build_backend_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_sdist_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    pbi_pre_built: bool = False,

    build_sdist_only: bool = False,
) -> Phase:
    wi = WorkItem(

        unpack_dir=unpack_dir,
        build_result=build_result,

        if build_backend_deps is not None

        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,
        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,
    )
    return _PHASE_TO_CLASS[phase](wi)

"""Requirement resolution for bootstrap process.

Handles PyPI and graph-based resolution strategies.
Git URL resolution stays in Bootstrapper (orchestration concern).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import threading
import typing

from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import NormalizedName, canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version

from . import finders, resolver, sources, wheels
from .dependency_graph import DependencyGraph
from .requirements_file import RequirementType

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from . import context

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class BootstrapRequirementResolver:
    """Resolve package requirements from PyPI or dependency graph during bootstrap.

    Single Responsibility: Coordinate resolution strategies for bootstrap process.
    Reason to Change: Resolution algorithm or provider priorities change.

    Resolution strategies (in order):
    1. Previous dependency graph (if available)
    2. PyPI lookup (via existing sources/resolver modules)

    Git URL resolution is NOT handled here - that stays in Bootstrapper
    because it requires BuildEnvironment and build dependencies.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        ctx: context.WorkContext,
        prev_graph: DependencyGraph | None = None,
        multiple_versions: bool = False,
        cache_wheel_server_url: str = "",
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize requirement resolver.

        Args:
            ctx: Work context with constraints and settings
            prev_graph: Optional previous dependency graph for caching
            multiple_versions: If ``True`` and no results are found through
                any other approach, takes the latest candidate from the
                cache server, ignoring the age filters.  In all other
                cases, returns an empty list when no candidates are found.
            cache_wheel_server_url: URL of the remote wheel cache server.
                Used as a fallback when age filtering produces no candidates.
        """
        self.ctx = ctx
        self.prev_graph = prev_graph
        self.multiple_versions = multiple_versions
        self.cache_wheel_server_url = cache_wheel_server_url
        # All known versions for a package, accumulated across resolution
        # contexts.  Versions discovered via different specifiers or req_types
        # are merged so that later lookups see the widest set.
        # Key: (normalized_name, pre_built)
        # Value: {version: url}
        self._known_versions: dict[tuple[NormalizedName, bool], dict[Version, str]] = {}
        # Requirement rules already resolved from network/graph.
        # Key: (str(req), pre_built)
        # Prevents redundant network calls for the same specifier.
        self._resolved_rules: set[tuple[str, bool]] = set()
        # Protects _known_versions and _resolved_rules for thread safety.
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def resolve(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
        req_type: RequirementType,
        parent_req: Requirement | None = None,
        pre_built: bool | None = None,
        return_all_versions: bool = False,
    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:
        """Resolve package requirement to matching version(s).

        Uses a two-step strategy:
        1. If this requirement rule has not been resolved before, fetch
           versions from the network (or previous graph) and extend the
           package-level known-versions cache.
        2. Filter all known versions for the package by the current
           requirement specifier.

        This ensures that versions discovered in one context (e.g.,
        top-level with cooldown bypass) are visible to later lookups
        with different specifiers for the same package.

        Args:
            req: Package requirement
            req_type: Type of requirement
            parent_req: Parent requirement from dependency chain
            pre_built: Optional override to force prebuilt (True) or source (False).
                If None (default), uses package build info to determine.
            return_all_versions: If True, return all matching versions. If False,
                return only the highest matching version.

        Returns:
            List of (url, version) tuples sorted by version (highest first).
            Contains one item when return_all_versions=False, or all matching
            versions when return_all_versions=True.

        """
        # Determine pre_built if not specified (needed for cache key)
        if pre_built is None:
            pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)
            pre_built = pbi.pre_built

        rule_key = (str(req), pre_built)

        with self._lock:
            if rule_key not in self._resolved_rules:
                # Rule not seen before — resolve from graph or network and
                # extend the package-level known-versions cache.
                self._resolve_and_extend(req, req_type, pre_built, parent_req)
                self._resolved_rules.add(rule_key)
            else:
                logger.debug(f"rule already resolved: {req}")

            # Filter all known versions by the current requirement specifier.
            matching = self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)

        if not matching:
            return []
        if return_all_versions:
            return matching
        return [matching[0]]

    def get_cached_resolution(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
        pre_built: bool,
    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]] | None:
        """Return cached matching versions if this requirement was already resolved.

        Returns ``None`` if the requirement has not been resolved yet, allowing
        callers to distinguish between "no matching versions" and "not yet resolved".

        Args:
            req: Package requirement
            pre_built: Whether looking for prebuilt or source resolution

        Returns:
            List of (url, version) tuples if previously resolved, None otherwise.
        """
        rule_key = (str(req), pre_built)
        with self._lock:
            if rule_key in self._resolved_rules:
                return self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)
        return None

    def _resolve_and_extend(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
        req_type: RequirementType,
        pre_built: bool,
        parent_req: Requirement | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Resolve versions from graph/network and extend known versions cache."""
        # Try previous dependency graph
        cached_resolution = self._resolve_from_graph(
            req=req,
            req_type=req_type,
            pre_built=pre_built,
            parent_req=parent_req,
        )

        if cached_resolution:
            logger.debug(
                f"resolved from previous bootstrap: {len(cached_resolution)} version(s)"
            )
            results = cached_resolution
        elif pre_built:
            # Resolve prebuilt wheel
            wheel_server_urls = wheels.get_wheel_server_urls(
                self.ctx, req, cache_wheel_server_url=resolver.PYPI_SERVER_URL
            )
            results = wheels.resolve_all_prebuilt_wheels(
                ctx=self.ctx,
                req=req,
                wheel_server_urls=wheel_server_urls,
                req_type=req_type,
            )
        else:
            # Resolve source (sdist)
            provider = sources.get_source_provider(
                ctx=self.ctx,
                req=req,
                sdist_server_url=resolver.PYPI_SERVER_URL,
                req_type=req_type,
            )

# Based on https://github.com/sarugaku/resolvelib/blob/main/examples/pypi_wheel_provider.py
#
# Modified to look at sdists instead of wheels and to avoid trying to
# resolve any dependencies.
#
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime
import enum
import functools
import logging
import os
import re
import typing
from collections.abc import Iterable
from operator import attrgetter
from platform import python_version
from urllib.parse import quote, urlparse

import pypi_simple
import resolvelib
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.specifiers import InvalidSpecifier, SpecifierSet
from packaging.tags import Tag, sys_tags
from packaging.utils import (
    BuildTag,
    canonicalize_name,
    parse_wheel_filename,
)
from packaging.version import Version
from requests.models import Response
from resolvelib.resolvers import RequirementInformation

from . import overrides
from .candidate import Candidate, Cooldown
from .constraints import Constraints
from .downloads import extract_filename_from_url as extract_filename_from_url
from .extras_provider import ExtrasProvider
from .http_retry import RETRYABLE_EXCEPTIONS, retry_on_exception
from .request_session import session
from .requirements_file import RequirementType
from .versionmap import VersionMap

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from . import context


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

PYTHON_VERSION = Version(python_version())
DEBUG_RESOLVER = os.environ.get("DEBUG_RESOLVER", "")
PYPI_SERVER_URL = "https://pypi.org/simple"
GITHUB_URL = "https://github.com"

# all supported tags
SUPPORTED_TAGS: frozenset[Tag] = frozenset(sys_tags())
# same, but ignore the platform for 'ignore_platform' flag
IGNORE_PLATFORM: str = "ignore"
SUPPORTED_TAGS_IGNORE_PLATFORM: frozenset[Tag] = frozenset(
    Tag(t.interpreter, t.abi, IGNORE_PLATFORM) for t in SUPPORTED_TAGS
)


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=200)
def match_py_req(py_req: str, *, python_version: Version = PYTHON_VERSION) -> bool:
    """Python version requirement lookup with LRU cache

    Raises InvalidSpecifier on error

    SpecifierSet parsing and matching takes a non-trivial amount of time. A
    bootstrap run can spend over 10% of its time in parsing and matching
    Python version requirements.

    This function caches the result of SpecifierSet parsing and contains
    operation for Python version requirement. Most packages share similar
    constraints, e.g. ``>= 3.10``.
    """
    return python_version in SpecifierSet(py_req)


def resolve(
    *,
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_server_url: str,
    include_sdists: bool = True,
    include_wheels: bool = True,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
    ignore_platform: bool = False,
) -> tuple[str, Version]:
    """Resolve requirement and return the best matching version.

    Returns (url, version) tuple for the highest matching version.
    """
    # Create the (reusable) resolver.
    provider = overrides.find_and_invoke(
        req.name,
        "get_resolver_provider",
        default_resolver_provider,
        ctx=ctx,
        req=req,
        include_sdists=include_sdists,
        include_wheels=include_wheels,
        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,
        req_type=req_type,
        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,
    )
    provider.cooldown = resolve_package_cooldown(ctx, req, req_type=req_type)
    max_age_cutoff = _compute_max_age_cutoff(ctx)
    results = find_all_matching_from_provider(
        provider, req, max_age_cutoff=max_age_cutoff
    )
    return results[0]


def default_resolver_provider(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    sdist_server_url: str,
    include_sdists: bool,
    include_wheels: bool,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
    ignore_platform: bool = False,
) -> (
    PyPIProvider
    | GenericProvider
    | GitHubTagProvider
    | GitLabTagProvider
    | VersionMapProvider
):
    """Lookup resolver provider to resolve package versions"""
    return PyPIProvider(
        include_sdists=include_sdists,
        include_wheels=include_wheels,
        sdist_server_url=sdist_server_url,
        constraints=ctx.constraints,
        req_type=req_type,
        ignore_platform=ignore_platform,
    )


def _has_equality_pin(req: Requirement) -> bool:
    """Return True if the requirement has a single exact ``==`` pin.

    Rejects wildcard pins (``==1.*``) and compound specifiers (``==1,>2``)
    which are not true exact version pins.
    """
    specs = list(req.specifier)
    return len(specs) == 1 and specs[0].operator == "==" and "*" not in specs[0].version


def resolve_package_cooldown(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
    req: Requirement,
    req_type: RequirementType | None = None,
) -> Cooldown | None:
    """Compute the effective cooldown for a single package.

    Args:
        ctx: The current work context (provides the global cooldown).
        req: The package requirement being resolved.
        req_type: The requirement type (top-level, install, etc.).

    Returns:
        The cooldown to pass to the provider, or ``None`` if disabled.
    """
    if req_type == RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL and _has_equality_pin(req):
        if ctx.cooldown is not None:
            logger.info("cooldown bypassed as the top-level requirement uses == pin")
        return None

    per_package_days = ctx.package_build_info(req).resolver_min_release_age
    global_cooldown = ctx.cooldown
    if per_package_days is None:
        return global_cooldown
    if per_package_days == 0:
        return None
    # Per-package positive override: inherit bootstrap_time from global so all
    # resolutions in a single run share the same fixed cutoff point.
    bootstrap_time = (
        global_cooldown.bootstrap_time
        if global_cooldown is not None
        else datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
    )
    return Cooldown(
        min_age=datetime.timedelta(days=per_package_days),
        bootstrap_time=bootstrap_time,
    )


def _compute_max_age_cutoff(
    ctx: context.WorkContext,
) -> datetime.datetime | None:
    """Compute the cutoff time for max release age filtering.

    Returns the oldest acceptable upload time, or None if disabled.
    Uses the cooldown's bootstrap_time for consistency across a single run.
    """
    if ctx.max_release_age is None:
        return None

{"type": "user", "message": {"role": "user", "content": "This is the fromager repository (Python wheel builder). A virtualenv with the project\nand test dependencies is already set up at `.venv`; run tests with\n`.venv/bin/python -m pytest -o addopts=\"\" tests/...`.\n\nImplement the following change to the resolver's max-release-age handling\n(`src/fromager/resolver.py`, `find_all_matching_from_provider()`, and its callers in\n`src/fromager/bootstrap_requirement_resolver.py`).\n\n1. Replace the boolean `fallback_on_empty_age_filter` parameter of\n   `find_all_matching_from_provider()` with an `AgeFallback` enum (exported from\n   `fromager.resolver`) selecting what happens when age filtering removes every candidate:\n   - `AgeFallback.ALL`: keep every candidate (this is the single-version default and the\n     current behaviour, including its \"keeping all to avoid empty resolution\" warning)\n   - `AgeFallback.NEWEST`: keep only the single newest candidate (new)\n   - `AgeFallback.NONE`: return an empty list\n   Name the new keyword parameter `age_fallback`, default `AgeFallback.ALL`.\n   Log on the `fromager.resolver` logger when the fallback triggers, with these exact\n   messages (`%s`/`%d` formatting, `name` is `req.name`):\n   - ALL, warning: `\"%s: all %d candidate(s) of %s are older than %d days, keeping all to avoid empty resolution\"`\n   - NEWEST, info: `\"%s: all %d candidate(s) of %s are older than %d days, falling back to newest version %s\"`\n   - NONE, info: `\"%s: all %d candidate(s) of %s are older than %d days\"`\n   Multi-version bootstrap mode must use `AgeFallback.NEWEST`, so that when a dependency\n   has no release inside the age window (bar from two years ago depended on by a recent\n   foo) its newest version is built instead of failing, which avoids cascading failures\n   in the dependent package.\n\n2. Packages whose constraint pins an exact version (the provider's `constraints` object\n   returns a constraint for the requirement name and that constraint is a single `==`\n   specifier) skip age filtering entirely. A pin is explicit user intent and must not be\n   overridden by the age heuristic. Range constraints (`>=`, `<`, `!=`, ...) are still\n   age-filtered like unconstrained packages. Log at INFO on the\n   `fromager.resolver` logger: `\"%s: skipping age filter for pinned constraint (%d candidate(s))\"`.\n   Previously, in multi-version mode a constrained package pinned to a version older than\n   the window lost every candidate and resolution failed silently; in single-version mode\n   the fallback kept all candidates but logged the misleading warning.\n\nUpdate docstrings, add tests in `tests/test_cooldown.py` and\n`tests/test_bootstrap_requirement_resolver.py`, and run both files."}, "timestamp": "2026-10-09T15:58:12.589Z"}

Returns list of (url, version) tuples sorted by version (highest first).\n\n    IMPORTANT: This bypasses resolvelib's full resolver to collect all matching\n    candidates. """Tests for bootstrap_requirement_resolver module."""

from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager import resolver
from fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver import BootstrapRequirementResolver
from fromager.context import WorkContext
from fromager.dependency_graph import DependencyGraph
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType

# Test fixture: previous dependency graph
old_graph = DependencyGraph()

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=None,
    parent_version=None,
    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
    req=Requirement("foo"),
    req_version=Version("1.0.0"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=canonicalize_name("foo"),
    parent_version=Version("1.0.0"),
    req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
    req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
    req_version=Version("7"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=None,
    parent_version=None,
    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
    req=Requirement("bar"),
    req_version=Version("1.0.0"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=canonicalize_name("bar"),
    parent_version=Version("1.0.0"),
    req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
    req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
    req_version=Version("6"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=None,
    parent_version=None,
    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
    req=Requirement("blah"),
    req_version=Version("1.0.0"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=canonicalize_name("blah"),
    parent_version=Version("1.0.0"),
    req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
    req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
    req_version=Version("5"),
)


def test_resolve_from_graph_no_changes(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver resolves from previous graph with no changes."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Resolving new dependency that doesn't exist in graph
    assert (
        resolver._resolve_from_graph(
            req=Requirement("xyz"),
            req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
            pre_built=False,
            parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
        )
        is None
    )

    # Resolving pbr dependency of foo
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
    ) == [("", Version("7"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of bar
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("bar"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of blah
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("blah"),
    ) == [("", Version("5"))]


def test_resolve_from_graph_install_dep_upgrade(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver prefers top-level requirements over history."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Simulating new bootstrap with a toplevel requirement of pbr==8
    tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
        parent_name=None,
        parent_version=None,
        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
        req=Requirement("pbr==8"),
        req_version=Version("8"),
    )

    # Resolving pbr dependency of foo - should get upgraded version from top-level
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
    ) == [("", Version("8"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of bar - constraint prevents upgrade
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("bar"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of blah - exact version requirement
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("blah"),
    ) == [("", Version("5"))]


def test_resolve_from_graph_install_dep_downgrade(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver handles version downgrades from top-level requirements."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Simulating new bootstrap with a toplevel requirement of pbr<=6
    tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
        parent_name=None,
        parent_version=None,
        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
        req=Requirement("pbr<=6"),
        req_version=Version("6"),
    )

    # Resolving pbr dependency of foo - gets downgraded to 6
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of bar - already at 6
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("bar"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of blah - exact version requirement
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("blah"),
    ) == [("", Version("5"))]


def test_resolve_from_graph_toplevel_dep(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver resolves top-level dependencies correctly."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Simulating new bootstrap with a toplevel requirement for foo
    tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
        parent_name=None,

        req=Requirement("foo==2"),

    )

    # Simulating new bootstrap with a toplevel requirement of bar (no change)
    tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
        parent_name=None,
        parent_version=None,

"""Tests for the release-age cooldown policy (issue #877).

The cooldown rejects package versions published fewer than N days ago,
protecting against supply-chain attacks where a malicious version is
published and immediately pulled in by automated builds.
"""

import datetime
import logging
import pathlib
import re
import typing

import pytest
import requests_mock
import resolvelib
import yaml
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager import (
    candidate,
    constraints,
    context,
    packagesettings,
    resolver,
    sources,
    wheels,
)
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType

_BOOTSTRAP_TIME = datetime.datetime(2026, 3, 26, 0, 0, 0, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)
_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS = datetime.timedelta(days=7)
# cutoff = 2026-03-19T00:00:00Z

# Use PEP 691 JSON format — pypi_simple reliably parses upload-time from JSON.
_PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE = "application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json"

# Three versions at known ages:
#   2.0.0  uploaded 2026-03-24 →  2 days old (within cooldown)
#   1.3.2  uploaded 2026-03-15 → 11 days old (outside cooldown)
#   1.2.2  uploaded 2026-01-01 → 84 days old (outside cooldown)
_cooldown_json_response = {
    "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
    "name": "test-pkg",
    "files": [
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-24T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "bbb"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-15T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "ccc"},
            "upload-time": "2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
    ],
}

_all_recent_json_response = {
    "meta": {"api-version": "1.1"},
    "name": "test-pkg",
    "files": [
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "aaa"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-25T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
        {
            "filename": "test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "url": "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/test_pkg-1.3.2-py3-none-any.whl",
            "hashes": {"sha256": "bbb"},
            "upload-time": "2026-03-24T00:00:00+00:00",
        },
    ],
}

_COOLDOWN = candidate.Cooldown(
    min_age=_COOLDOWN_7_DAYS,
    bootstrap_time=_BOOTSTRAP_TIME,
)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def clear_resolver_cache() -> typing.Generator[None, None, None]:
    """Clear the class-level resolver cache before each test.

    BaseProvider.resolver_cache is a ClassVar that persists across test
    instances. Without clearing it, candidates fetched in one test are reused
    by subsequent tests, bypassing mocked HTTP responses and producing
    incorrect results.
    """
    resolver.BaseProvider.clear_cache()
    resolver.BaseProvider._cooldown_unsupported_warned.clear()
    yield


def test_cooldown_filters_recent_version(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """Versions within the cooldown window are skipped; older ones are selected."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
            result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        # 2.0.0 is 2 days old (within cooldown); 1.3.2 is 11 days old (outside).
        assert str(candidate.version) == "1.3.2"
        # 2.0.0 should be logged as blocked; 1.3.2 should not appear in the summary.
        assert "cooldown blocked 1 version(s): 2.0.0" in caplog.text


def test_cooldown_disabled_selects_latest() -> None:
    """Without a cooldown the resolver selects the latest version as normal."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_cooldown_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=None)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())
        result = rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        candidate = result.mapping["test-pkg"]
        assert str(candidate.version) == "2.0.0"


def test_cooldown_all_blocked_raises_informative_error() -> None:
    """When all candidates are within the cooldown window the error says so."""
    with requests_mock.Mocker() as r:
        r.get(
            "https://pypi.org/simple/test-pkg/",
            json=_all_recent_json_response,
            headers={"Content-Type": _PYPI_SIMPLE_JSON_CONTENT_TYPE},
        )
        provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(include_sdists=True, cooldown=_COOLDOWN)
        rslvr = resolvelib.Resolver(provider, resolvelib.BaseReporter())

        with pytest.raises(resolvelib.resolvers.ResolverException) as exc_info:
            rslvr.resolve([Requirement("test-pkg")])

        msg = str(exc_info.value)
        assert "2 candidate(s)" in msg
        assert "published within the last 7 days (release-age cooldown" in msg


def test_cooldown_rejects_candidate_without_upload_time(
    caplog: pytest.LogCaptureFixture,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    """A candidate with no upload_time is rejected when a cooldown is active (fail closed)."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(resolver, "DEBUG_RESOLVER", "1")
    candidate = resolver.Candidate(
        name="test-pkg",
        version=Version("1.0.0"),
        url="https://example.com/test-pkg-1.0.0.tar.gz",
        upload_time=None,
    )
    provider = resolver.PyPIProvider(cooldown=_COOLDOWN)

    with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG, logger="fromager.resolver"):
        result = provider.is_blocked_by_cooldown(candidate)

    assert result is True
    assert "upload_time unknown" in caplog.text
    assert "1.0.0" in caplog.text
