          \n\u001b[38;2;0;0;0m  \u001b[0m\n💡 tldr <cmd> — quick examples for any command (better than man pages)\n\n\"\"\"Discount rules applied per line.\"\"\"\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom decimal import Decimal\n\nfrom .money import round_money\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Discount:\n    code: str\n    percent: Decimal  # 0..100\n\n\ndef percent_off(code: str, pct: str | Decimal) -> Discount:\n    return Discount(code, Decimal(pct))\n\n\ndef apply_discount(amount: Decimal, discount: Discount | None) -> Decimal:\n    \"\"\"Return the discounted line amount, rounded to cents.\"\"\"\n    if discount is None:\n        return round_money(amount)\n    factor = (Decimal(100) - discount.percent) / Decimal(100)\n    return round_money(amount * factor)\n\"\"\"Invoice model.\"\"\"\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom decimal import Decimal\n\nfrom .discounts import Discount\nfrom .tax import TaxRule\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass LineItem:\n    sku: str\n    unit_price: Decimal\n    qty: int\n    discount: Discount | None = None\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Invoice:\n    number: str\n    lines: list[LineItem] = field(default_factory=list)\n    tax_rule: TaxRule | None = None\n\n    def add(self, sku: str, unit_price: str | Decimal, qty: int = 1, discount: Discount | None = None) -> \"Invoice\":\n        self.lines.append(LineItem(sku, Decimal(unit_price), qty, discount))\n        return self\n\n\ndef build_invoice(number: str, rows: list[tuple], tax_rule: TaxRule | None = None) -> Invoice:\n    inv = Invoice(number, tax_rule=tax_rule)\n    for row in rows:\n        inv.add(*row)\n    return inv\n\"\"\"Money helpers. All amounts are Decimal with two places, or int cents.\"\"\"\nfrom decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP\n\nTWO = Decimal(\"0.01\")\n\n\ndef round_money(x: Decimal) -> Decimal:\n    return x.quantize(TWO, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)\n\n\ndef to_cents(x: Decimal) -> int:\n    return int(round_money(x) * 100)\n\n\ndef from_cents(c: int) -> Decimal:\n    return Decimal(c) / 100\n\"\"\"Tax rules.\"\"\"\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom decimal import Decimal\n\nfrom .money import round_money\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass TaxRule:\n    region: str\n    rate: Decimal  # e.g. Decimal(\"0.19\")\n\n\ndef tax_for(amount: Decimal, rule: TaxRule | None) -> Decimal:\n    if rule is None:\n        return Decimal(\"0.00\")\n    return round_money(amount * rule.rate)\n\"\"\"Totals. The PDF renderer shows line_totals(); the amount charged is invoice_total().\"\"\"\nfrom decimal import Decimal\n\nfrom .discounts import apply_discount\nfrom .invoice import Invoice\nfrom .money import round_money\nfrom .tax import tax_for\n\n\ndef line_totals(inv: Invoice) -> list[Decimal]:\n    \"\"\"Per-line amounts as printed on the invoice, discount applied per line.\"\"\"\n    return [apply_discount(li.unit_price * li.qty, li.discount) for li in inv.lines]\n\n\ndef invoice_total(inv: Invoice) -> Decimal:\n    \"\"\"Amount charged: sum of lines after discount, plus tax on that sum.\"\"\"\n    gross = sum((li.unit_price * li.qty for li in inv.lines), Decimal(\"0\"))\n    discount_amount = Decimal(\"0\")\n    for li in inv.lines:\n        if li.discount is not None:\n            discount_amount += li.unit_price * li.qty * li.discount.percent / Decimal(100)\n    net = round_money(gross - discount_amount)\n    return round_money(net + tax_for(net, inv.tax_rule))\n\"\"\"Plain-text invoice renderer used by the PDF pipeline.\"\"\"\nfrom .invoice import Invoice\nfrom .totals import line_totals, invoice_total\n\n\ndef render(inv: Invoice) -> str:\n    rows = [f\"{li.sku:12} {li.qty:>3} x {li.unit_price:>8}  {amt:>10}\" for li, amt in zip(inv.lines, line_totals(inv))]\n    rows.append(f\"{'TOTAL':>38} {invoice_total(inv):>10}\")\n    return \"\\n\".join(rows)\nfrom .invoice import Invoice, LineItem, build_invoice\nfrom .money import to_cents, from_cents, round_money\nfrom .discounts import apply_discount, percent_off, Discount\nfrom .tax import tax_for, TaxRule\nfrom .totals import invoice_total, line_totals\n\n__all__ = [\"Invoice\", \"LineItem\", \"build_invoice\", \"to_cents\", \"from_cents\", \"round_money\",\n           \"apply_discount\", \"percent_off\", \"Discount\", \"tax_for\", \"TaxRule\", \"invoice_total\", \"line_totals\"]\nfrom decimal import Decimal\n\nfrom billing import build_invoice, percent_off, invoice_total, line_totals, TaxRule\n\n\ndef test_simple_total():\n    inv = build_invoice(\"A1\", [(\"x\", \"10.00\", 2), (\"y\", \"0.50\", 1)])\n    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal(\"20.50\")\n    assert sum(line_totals(inv)) == Decimal(\"20.50\")\n\n\ndef test_with_tax():\n    inv = build_invoice(\"A2\", [(\"x\", \"100.00\", 1)], TaxRule(\"DE\", Decimal(\"0.19\")))\n    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal(\"119.00\")\n\n\ndef test_discount_whole_numbers():\n    inv = build_invoice(\"A3\", [(\"x\", \"100.00\", 1, percent_off(\"TEN\", \"10\"))])\n    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal(\"90.00\")","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_017arE6MbrY6e9CqBHK1Jvdq","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"rule"}}]}

The full suite passes (4 tests), and the new regression test fails on the old code.\n\n**Root cause:** `invoice_total()` in `billing/totals.py` didn't add up the line amounts the PDF prints. It added up the unrounded gross and the unrounded discount amounts, then rounded once at the end. `line_totals()`, which the PDF uses, rounds each line after its discount. Whenever several discounted lines each carry a half-cent remainder, the two methods disagree by a cent. For example, two lines of 1.10 at 15% off print as 0.94 + 0.94 = 1.88, but the old code charged 1.87. Nothing raises an error, which is why the logs were clean.\n\n**Fix:** `invoice_total()` now takes `net = sum(line_totals(inv))`, so the charged amount is the sum of the printed lines. Tax is still computed on that net. The public API is unchanged.\n\n**Test:** I added `test_total_matches_sum_of_rounded_lines_with_discounts` to `tests/test_billing.py`.\n\n- **Tracked `.pyc` files:** They show as modified in `git status` because pytest rewrote them. from decimal import Decimal

from billing import build_invoice, percent_off, invoice_total, line_totals, TaxRule


def test_simple_total():
    inv = build_invoice("A1", [("x", "10.00", 2), ("y", "0.50", 1)])
    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal("20.50")
    assert sum(line_totals(inv)) == Decimal("20.50")


def test_with_tax():
    inv = build_invoice("A2", [("x", "100.00", 1)], TaxRule("DE", Decimal("0.19")))
    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal("119.00")


def test_discount_whole_numbers():
    inv = build_invoice("A3", [("x", "100.00", 1, percent_off("TEN", "10"))])
    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal("90.00")


def test_total_matches_sum_of_rounded_lines_with_discounts():
    # each line: 1.10 * 0.85 = 0.935 -> 0.94; the old aggregate math gave 2.20 * 0.85 = 1.87
    d = percent_off("D", "15")
    inv = build_invoice("A4", [("x", "1.10", 1, d), ("y", "1.10", 1, d)])
    assert sum(line_totals(inv)) == Decimal("1.88")
    assert invoice_total(inv) == Decimal("1.88")

"""Totals. The PDF renderer shows line_totals(); the amount charged is invoice_total()."""
from decimal import Decimal

from .discounts import apply_discount
from .invoice import Invoice
from .money import round_money
from .tax import tax_for


def line_totals(inv: Invoice) -> list[Decimal]:
    """Per-line amounts as printed on the invoice, discount applied per line."""
    return [apply_discount(li.unit_price * li.qty, li.discount) for li in inv.lines]


def invoice_total(inv: Invoice) -> Decimal:
    """Amount charged: sum of lines after discount, plus tax on that sum."""
    net = sum(line_totals(inv), Decimal("0"))
    return round_money(net + tax_for(net, inv.tax_rule))

import re
import unicodedata

_WS = re.compile(r"\s+")


def email_key(email):
    return email.strip().casefold()


def name_key(name):
    """Key for matching names: case-folded, single spaces, no accents."""
    s = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", name.casefold())
    s = "".join(c for c in s if not unicodedata.combining(c))
    # casefold again: NFKD can expose new foldable characters
    return _WS.sub(" ", s.casefold()).strip()


def dedupe(records):
    """records: list of dicts with 'name' and 'email'. Returns survivors in first-seen order."""
    seen_names, seen_emails, out = set(), set(), []
    for r in records:
        nk, ek = name_key(r["name"]), email_key(r["email"])
        if nk in seen_names or ek in seen_emails:
            continue
        seen_names.add(nk)
        seen_emails.add(ek)
        out.append(r)
    return out

import functools
import operator
import re
import sys


class ResolutionError(Exception):
    pass


@functools.total_ordering
class Version:
    def __init__(self, s):
        self._s = str(s).strip()
        try:
            parts = [int(p) for p in self._s.split(".")]
        except ValueError:
            raise ValueError(f"invalid version: {s!r}")
        while len(parts) > 1 and parts[-1] == 0:
            parts.pop()
        self._key = tuple(parts)

    def __eq__(self, other):
        return isinstance(other, Version) and self._key == other._key

    def __lt__(self, other):
        return self._key < other._key

    def __hash__(self):
        return hash(self._key)

    def __str__(self):
        return self._s

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Version({self._s!r})"


_OPS = {
    "==": operator.eq,
    "!=": operator.ne,
    "<=": operator.le,
    ">=": operator.ge,
    "<": operator.lt,
    ">": operator.gt,
}
_CON_RE = re.compile(r"^(==|!=|<=|>=|<|>)\s*(\S+)$")


class Constraint:
    def __init__(self, name, specs=()):
        self.name = name
        self.specs = tuple(specs)

    @classmethod
    def parse(cls, requirement):
        m = re.match(r"^\s*([^\s=!<>,]+)\s*(.*)$", requirement)
        if not m:
            raise ValueError(f"invalid requirement: {requirement!r}")
        name, rest = m.group(1), m.group(2).strip()
        specs = []
        if rest:
            for part in rest.split(","):
                cm = _CON_RE.match(part.strip())
                if not cm:
                    raise ValueError(f"invalid constraint: {part!r}")
                specs.append((cm.group(1), Version(cm.group(2))))
        return cls(name, specs)

    def allows(self, version):
        if not isinstance(version, Version):
            version = Version(version)
        return all(_OPS[op](version, v) for op, v in self.specs)


def resolve(roots, index):
    sys.setrecursionlimit(max(sys.getrecursionlimit(), 20000))
    versions = {
        n: sorted(((Version(v), v) for v in vs), key=lambda t: t[0], reverse=True)
        for n, vs in index.items()
    }
    parsed = {}

    def reqs(name, vstr):
        key = (name, vstr)
        if key not in parsed:
            parsed[key] = [Constraint.parse(r) for r in index[name][vstr]]
        return parsed[key]

    failed = []

    def candidates(name, cons):
        return [
            (v, s) for v, s in versions.get(name, ())
            if all(c.allows(v) for c in cons)
        ]

    def fail(name):
        if not failed:
            failed.append(name)

    def search(chosen, cons):
        pending = sorted(n for n in cons if n not in chosen)
        if not pending:
            return chosen
        name = pending[0]
        for v, s in candidates(name, cons[name]):
            new_cons = {k: list(c) for k, c in cons.items()}
            ok = True
            for r in reqs(name, s):
                if r.name in chosen:
                    if not r.allows(chosen[r.name][0]):
                        fail(name)
                        ok = False
                        break
                    continue
                new_cons.setdefault(r.name, []).append(r)
                if not candidates(r.name, new_cons[r.name]):
                    fail(r.name)
                    ok = False
                    break
            if not ok:
                continue
            new_chosen = dict(chosen)
            new_chosen[name] = (v, s)
            res = search(new_chosen, new_cons)
            if res is not None:
                return res
        fail(name)
        return None

    cons = {}
    for r in roots:
        c = Constraint.parse(r)
        cons.setdefault(c.name, []).append(c)
    for n, cs in cons.items():
        if not candidates(n, cs):
            raise ResolutionError(f"no version of {n} satisfies constraints")
    res = search({}, cons)
    if res is None:
        raise ResolutionError(
            f"cannot satisfy constraints for package {failed[0] if failed else '?'}"
        )
    return {n: s for n, (v, s) in res.items()}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Nn8syzWnQtjvsByCvvoMTi","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Resolver spec\n2\t\n3\tIndex: `dict[str, dict[str, list[str]]]`, mapping package name to a mapping of version\n4\tstring to its list of requirement strings. Example:\n5\t\n6\t```python\n7\tINDEX = {\n8\t  \"app\":  {\"1.0\": [\"web>=2\", \"db\"]},\n9\t  \"web\":  {\"1.0\": [], \"2.0\": [\"json<3\"], \"2.1\": [\"json>=3\"]},\n10\t  \"json\": {\"2.0\": [], \"3.0\": []},\n11\t  \"db\":   {\"1.0\": [\"json<3\"]},\n12\t}\n13\t```\n14\t\n15\tRequirement string grammar: `name` optionally followed by a comma-separated list of\n16\tconstraints, each `<op><version>` with op in `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`.\n17\tExamples: `web`, `web>=2`, `json>=2,<3`, `db==1.0`.\n18\t\n19\tVersions: dotted integers, compared numerically component-wise, missing components are\n20\tzero (`1.0 == 1`, `1.10 > 1.9`).\n21\t\n22\t`resolve(roots: list[str], index) -> dict[str, str]` returns the chosen version for every\n23\tpackage in the transitive closure, such that:\n24\t\n25\t- every root requirement and every requirement of every chosen version is satisfied by the\n26\t  chosen version of that package (one version per package);\n27\t- preference: among all valid solutions, pick the one that is lexicographically greatest\n28\t  when packages are ordered by name and compared by version (i.e. the first package in\n29\t  alphabetical order gets the highest version it can, then the next, and so on);\n30\t- packages not reachable from the roots are not in the result;\n31\t- cycles in dependencies are fine (`a -> b -> a`);\n32\t- if no solution exists raise `ResolutionError` whose message names the package whose\n33\t  constraints could not be satisfied (the leaf where the search dead-ended, for example\n34\t  `b` when `a` requires `b<1` and only `b 1` and `b 2` exist), not only the root.\n35\t\n36\tCorrectness over speed, but the hidden tests include an index with a few hundred\n37\tversions where naive full enumeration will time out (60 s). Backtracking with\n38\tconstraint propagation is enough.\n39\t\n40\tAlso export `Version` (comparable, hashable, `str()` gives the original string) and\n41\t`Constraint.parse(\"json>=2,<3\")` with `.name` and `.allows(Version)`.\n42\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"0b8a5370-71f2-49bd-b742-c6646ff87435","uuid":"3a3051a6-33c7-4bc9-8099-ac0586c8658a","timestamp":"2026-10-09T16:05:23.669Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/alustosa/git/model-routing-eval/.work/agent-eval/2026-10-09-claude-sonnet-5-5-effort-low/cases/t14_dep_resolver/resolver/SPEC.md","content":"# Resolver spec\n\nIndex: `dict[str, dict[str, list[str]]]`, mapping package name to a mapping of version\nstring to its list of requirement strings. Example:\n\n```python\nINDEX = {\n  \"app\":  {\"1.0\": [\"web>=2\", \"db\"]},\n  \"web\":  {\"1.0\": [], \"2.0\": [\"json<3\"], \"2.1\": [\"json>=3\"]},\n  \"json\": {\"2.0\": [], \"3.0\": []},\n  \"db\":   {\"1.0\": [\"json<3\"]},\n}\n```\n\nRequirement string grammar: `name` optionally followed by a comma-separated list of\nconstraints, each `<op><version>` with op in `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`.\nExamples: `web`, `web>=2`, `json>=2,<3`, `db==1.0`.\n\nVersions: dotted integers, compared numerically component-wise, missing components are\nzero (`1.0 == 1`, `1.10 > 1.9`).\n\n`resolve(roots: list[str], index) -> dict[str, str]` returns the chosen version for every\npackage in the transitive closure, such that:\n\n- every root requirement and every requirement of every chosen version is satisfied by the\n  chosen version of that package (one version per package);\n- preference: among all valid solutions, pick the one that is lexicographically greatest\n  when packages are ordered by name and compared by version (i.e. the first package in\n  alphabetical order gets the highest version it can, then the next, and so on);\n- packages not reachable from the roots are not in the result;\n- cycles in dependencies are fine (`a -> b -> a`);\n- if no solution exists raise `ResolutionError` whose message names the package whose\n  constraints could not be satisfied (the leaf where the search dead-ended, for example\n  `b` when `a` requires `b<1` and only `b 1` and `b 2` exist), not only the root.\n\nCorrectness over speed, but the hidden tests include an index with a few hundred\nversions where naive full enumeration will time out (60 s). Backtracking with\nconstraint propagation is enough.\n\nAlso export `Version` (comparable, hashable, `str()` gives the original string) and\n`Constraint.parse(\"json>=2,<3\")` with `.name` and `.allows(Version)`.\n","numLines":42,"startLine":1,"totalLines":42}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01Nn8syzWnQtjvsByCvvoMTi","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"rule"}}]}

import os
import sys

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))
from resolver.solve import Constraint, ResolutionError, Version, resolve

INDEX = {
    "app": {"1.0": ["web>=2", "db"]},
    "web": {"1.0": [], "2.0": ["json<3"], "2.1": ["json>=3"]},
    "json": {"2.0": [], "3.0": []},
    "db": {"1.0": ["json<3"]},
}


def test_version():
    assert Version("1.0") == Version("1")
    assert Version("1.10") > Version("1.9")
    assert str(Version("1.0")) == "1.0"
    assert len({Version("1.0"), Version("1")}) == 1


def test_constraint():
    c = Constraint.parse("json>=2,<3")
    assert c.name == "json"
    assert c.allows(Version("2.5")) and not c.allows(Version("3"))


def test_basic():
    assert resolve(["app"], INDEX) == {"app": "1.0", "web": "2.0", "db": "1.0", "json": "2.0"}


def test_cycle():
    idx = {"a": {"1": ["b"]}, "b": {"1": ["a"]}}
    assert resolve(["a"], idx) == {"a": "1", "b": "1"}


def test_error_names_leaf():
    idx = {"a": {"1": ["b<1"]}, "b": {"1": [], "2": []}}
    with pytest.raises(ResolutionError, match="b"):
        resolve(["a"], idx)


def test_backtrack():
    idx = {"a": {"1": ["b==1"], "2": ["b==2"]}, "b": {"1": [], "2": ["c"]}, "c": {"1": ["a<2"]}}
    assert resolve(["a"], idx) == {"a": "1", "b": "1"}


def test_large():
    idx = {}
    for i in range(40):
        idx[f"p{i:02d}"] = {str(v): [f"p{i+1:02d}!={v}"] if i < 39 else [] for v in range(8)}
    r = resolve(["p00"], idx)
    assert len(r) == 40

"""Drop duplicate events (the collector retries, so the same event_id can appear several times).

Refactored to keep insertion order of first occurrence, which the old set-based version did not guarantee.
"""


def dedupe_rows(rows):
    seen_ids = set()
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        if r.event_id in seen_ids:
            continue
        seen_ids.add(r.event_id)
        out.append(r)
    return out

+
+from reporting import UsageRow, dedupe_rows
+
+

+    assert [r.event_id for r in dedupe_rows(rows)] == ["b", "a", "c"]

+def test_dedupe_scales_linearly():
+    # Quadratic dedupe takes tens of seconds at this size; linear takes milliseconds.
+    rows = [UsageRow(f"e{i}", "t", "s", 1.0, 1) for i in range(200_000)]
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    out = dedupe_rows(rows + rows[:1000])
+    assert len(out) == 200_000
+    assert time.perf_counter() - start < 2.0

branch\n\nfrom .model import UsageRow, parse_rows\nfrom .dedupe import dedupe_rows\nfrom .aggregate import aggregate\nfrom .report import build_report\n\n__all__ = [\"UsageRow\", \"parse_rows\", \"dedupe_rows\", \"aggregate\", \"build_report\"]\nfrom collections import defaultdict\n\n\ndef aggregate(rows):\n    \"\"\"Per (tenant, service): total cpu_seconds, total bytes_out, event count. Sorted by tenant then service.\"\"\"\n    acc = defaultdict(lambda: [0.0, 0, 0])\n    for r in rows:\n        a = acc[(r.tenant, r.service)]\n        a[0] += r.cpu_seconds\n        a[1] += r.bytes_out\n        a[2] += 1\n    return {k: tuple(v) for k, v in sorted(acc.items())}\n\"\"\"Drop duplicate events (the collector retries, so the same event_id can appear several times).\n\nRefactored to keep insertion order of first occurrence, which the old set-based version did not guarantee.\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef dedupe_rows(rows):\n    seen_ids = []\n    out = []\n    for r in rows:\n        if r.event_id in seen_ids:\n            continue\n        seen_ids.append(r.event_id)\n        out.append(r)\n    return out\nfrom .dedupe import dedupe_rows\nfrom .aggregate import aggregate\n\n\ndef build_report(rows):\n    \"\"\"Returns list of dicts, one per (tenant, service), plus a totals row at the end.\"\"\"\n    rows = dedupe_rows(rows)\n    agg = aggregate(rows)\n    out = []\n    tot_cpu, tot_bytes, tot_n = 0.0, 0, 0\n    for (tenant, service), (cpu, byts, n) in agg.items():\n        out.append({\"tenant\": tenant, \"service\": service, \"cpu_seconds\": round(cpu, 3), \"bytes_out\": byts, \"events\": n})\n        tot_cpu += cpu; tot_bytes += byts; tot_n += n\n    out.append({\"tenant\": \"*\", \"service\": \"*\", \"cpu_seconds\": round(tot_cpu, 3), \"bytes_out\": tot_bytes, \"events\": tot_n})\n    return out\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass UsageRow:\n    event_id: str\n    tenant: str\n    service: str\n    cpu_seconds: float\n    bytes_out: int\n\n\ndef parse_rows(lines):\n    \"\"\"lines: iterable of 'event_id,tenant,service,cpu_seconds,bytes_out'\"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    for line in lines:\n        line = line.strip()\n        if not line or line.startswith(\"#\"):\n            continue\n        e, t, s, c, b = line.split(\",\")\n        rows.append(UsageRow(e, t, s, float(c), int(b)))\n    return rows\nfrom reporting import parse_rows, build_report\n\n\ndef test_small_report():\n    rows = parse_rows([\"e1,acme,api,1.5,100\", \"e2,acme,api,0.5,50\", \"e2,acme,api,0.5,50\", \"e3,beta,web,2,10\"])\n    rep = build_report(rows)\n    assert rep[0] == {\"tenant\": \"acme\", \"service\": \"api\", \"cpu_seconds\": 2.0, \"bytes_out\": 150, \"events\": 2}\n    assert rep[-1][\"events\"] == 3","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01BihFAdKri3bwkp18RDtDff","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"rule"}}]}

import time

from reporting import UsageRow, dedupe_rows


def test_dedupe_preserves_first_occurrence_order():
    rows = [UsageRow(i, "t", "s", 1.0, 1) for i in ("b", "a", "b", "c", "a")]
    assert [r.event_id for r in dedupe_rows(rows)] == ["b", "a", "c"]


def test_dedupe_scales_linearly():
    # Quadratic dedupe takes tens of seconds at this size; linear takes milliseconds.
    rows = [UsageRow(f"e{i}", "t", "s", 1.0, 1) for i in range(200_000)]
    start = time.perf_counter()
    out = dedupe_rows(rows + rows[:1000])
    assert len(out) == 200_000
    assert time.perf_counter() - start < 2.0

import copy
import re


class PatchError(Exception):
    pass


class PointerError(PatchError):
    pass


_INDEX_RE = re.compile(r"(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\Z")


def _parse(pointer):
    if not isinstance(pointer, str):
        raise PointerError("pointer must be a string")
    if pointer == "":
        return []
    if not pointer.startswith("/"):
        raise PointerError(f"invalid pointer: {pointer!r}")
    return [t.replace("~1", "/").replace("~0", "~") for t in pointer[1:].split("/")]


def _index(token, length, allow_end):
    if token == "-" and allow_end:
        return length
    if not _INDEX_RE.match(token):
        raise PointerError(f"invalid array index: {token!r}")
    idx = int(token)
    if idx > length or (idx == length and not allow_end):
        raise PointerError(f"array index out of range: {token!r}")
    return idx


def _walk(doc, tokens):
    for t in tokens:
        if isinstance(doc, dict):
            if t not in doc:
                raise PointerError(f"missing key: {t!r}")
            doc = doc[t]
        elif isinstance(doc, list):
            doc = doc[_index(t, len(doc), False)]
        else:
            raise PointerError(f"cannot descend into scalar at {t!r}")
    return doc


def resolve_pointer(doc, pointer):
    return _walk(doc, _parse(pointer))


def _add(doc, tokens, value):
    if not tokens:
        return value
    parent = _walk(doc, tokens[:-1])
    last = tokens[-1]
    if isinstance(parent, dict):
        parent[last] = value
    elif isinstance(parent, list):
        parent.insert(_index(last, len(parent), True), value)
    else:
        raise PointerError("parent is not a container")
    return doc


def _remove(doc, tokens):
    """Return (new_doc, removed_value)."""
    if not tokens:
        raise PatchError("cannot remove the document root")
    parent = _walk(doc, tokens[:-1])
    last = tokens[-1]
    if isinstance(parent, dict):
        if last not in parent:
            raise PointerError(f"missing key: {last!r}")
        return doc, parent.pop(last)
    if isinstance(parent, list):
        return doc, parent.pop(_index(last, len(parent), False))
    raise PointerError("parent is not a container")


def _equal(a, b):
    if isinstance(a, bool) or isinstance(b, bool):
        return isinstance(a, bool) and isinstance(b, bool) and a == b
    if isinstance(a, dict) and isinstance(b, dict):
        return a.keys() == b.keys() and all(_equal(a[k], b[k]) for k in a)
    if isinstance(a, list) and isinstance(b, list):
        return len(a) == len(b) and all(_equal(x, y) for x, y in zip(a, b))
    if isinstance(a, (dict, list)) or isinstance(b, (dict, list)):
        return False
    return type(a) is type(b) or (
        isinstance(a, (int, float)) and isinstance(b, (int, float))
    ) and a == b


def _apply_op(doc, op):
    if not isinstance(op, dict):
        raise PatchError("operation must be an object")
    name = op.get("op")
    if name not in ("add", "remove", "replace", "move", "copy", "test"):
        raise PatchError(f"unknown op: {name!r}")
    if not isinstance(op.get("path"), str):
        raise PatchError("missing or invalid 'path'")
    tokens = _parse(op["path"])
    if name in ("add", "replace", "test") and "value" not in op:
        raise PatchError("missing 'value'")
    if name in ("move", "copy"):
        if not isinstance(op.get("from"), str):
            raise PatchError("missing or invalid 'from'")
        src = _parse(op["from"])

    if name == "add":
        return _add(doc, tokens, copy.deepcopy(op["value"]))
    if name == "remove":
        return _remove(doc, tokens)[0]
    if name == "replace":
        _walk(doc, tokens)  # must exist
        if not tokens:
            return copy.deepcopy(op["value"])
        doc, _ = _remove(doc, tokens)
        return _add(doc, tokens, copy.deepcopy(op["value"]))
    if name == "test":
        if not _equal(_walk(doc, tokens), op["value"]):
            raise PatchError("test failed")
        return doc
    if name == "copy":
        value = copy.deepcopy(_walk(doc, src))
        return _add(doc, tokens, value)
    # move
    _walk(doc, src)
    if len(src) < len(tokens) and tokens[: len(src)] == src:
        raise PatchError("cannot move a value into its own child")
    if src == tokens:
        return doc
    doc, value = _remove(doc, src)
    return _add(doc, tokens, value)


def apply_patch(doc, patch, in_place=False):
    if not isinstance(patch, list):
        raise PatchError("patch must be a list")
    work = copy.deepcopy(doc)
    for op in patch:
        try:
            work = _apply_op(work, op)
        except PatchError:
            raise
        except (TypeError, ValueError, KeyError, IndexError) as e:
            raise PatchError(str(e)) from e
    if in_place:
        if isinstance(doc, dict) and isinstance(work, dict):
            doc.clear()
            doc.update(work)
            return doc
        if isinstance(doc, list) and isinstance(work, list):
            doc[:] = work
            return doc
    return work

+import copy

 class PatchError(Exception):

     pass
 
 
+_INDEX_RE = re.compile(r"(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\Z")
+
+
+def _parse(pointer):
+    if not isinstance(pointer, str):
+        raise PointerError("pointer must be a string")
+    if pointer == "":
+        return []
+    if not pointer.startswith("/"):
+        raise PointerError(f"invalid pointer: {pointer!r}")
+    return [t.replace("~1", "/").replace("~0", "~") for t in pointer[1:].split("/")]
+
+
+def _index(token, length, allow_end):
+    if token == "-" and allow_end:
+        return length
+    if not _INDEX_RE.match(token):
+        raise PointerError(f"invalid array index: {token!r}")
+    idx = int(token)
+    if idx > length or (idx == length and not allow_end):
+        raise PointerError(f"array index out of range: {token!r}")
+    return idx
+
+
+def _walk(doc, tokens):
+    for t in tokens:
+        if isinstance(doc, dict):
+            if t not in doc:
+                raise PointerError(f"missing key: {t!r}")
+            doc = doc[t]
+        elif isinstance(doc, list):
+            doc = doc[_index(t, len(doc), False)]
+        else:
+            raise PointerError(f"cannot descend into scalar at {t!r}")
+    return doc
+
+

-    raise NotImplementedError
+    return _walk(doc, _parse(pointer))
+
+
+def _add(doc, tokens, value):
+    if not tokens:
+        return value
+    parent = _walk(doc, tokens[:-1])
+    last = tokens[-1]
+    if isinstance(parent, dict):
+        parent[last] = value
+    elif isinstance(parent, list):
+        parent.insert(_index(last, len(parent), True), value)
+    else:
+        raise PointerError("parent is not a container")
+    return doc
+
+
+def _remove(doc, tokens):
+    """Return (new_doc, removed_value)."""
+    if not tokens:
+        raise PatchError("cannot remove the document root")
+    parent = _walk(doc, tokens[:-1])
+    last = tokens[-1]
+    if isinstance(parent, dict):

+        return doc, parent.pop(last)
+    if isinstance(parent, list):
+        return doc, parent.pop(_index(last, len(parent), False))
+    raise PointerError("parent is not a container")
+
+
+def _equal(a, b):
+    if isinstance(a, bool) or isinstance(b, bool):
+        return isinstance(a, bool) and isinstance(b, bool) and a == b
+    if isinstance(a, dict) and isinstance(b, dict):
+        return a.keys() == b.keys() and all(_equal(a[k], b[k]) for k in a)
+    if isinstance(a, list) and isinstance(b, list):
+        return len(a) == len(b) and all(_equal(x, y) for x, y in zip(a, b))
+    if isinstance(a, (dict, list)) or isinstance(b, (dict, list)):
+        return False
+    return type(a) is type(b) or (
+        isinstance(a, (int, float)) and isinstance(b, (int, float))
+    ) and a == b

+
+def _apply_op(doc, op):

+import pytest

import copy
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
from jsonpatch.core import PatchError, PointerError, apply_patch, resolve_pointer


def test_pointer():
    d = {"a/b": [1, {"m~n": 2}], "": 5}
    assert resolve_pointer(d, "") is d
    assert resolve_pointer(d, "/a~1b/1/m~0n") == 2
    assert resolve_pointer(d, "/") == 5
    for bad in ["a", "/a~1b/01", "/a~1b/-", "/a~1b/2", "/nope", "/a~1b/x", "/a~1b/0/x"]:
        with pytest.raises(PointerError):
            resolve_pointer(d, bad)


def test_add_variants():
    assert apply_patch({}, [{"op": "add", "path": "", "value": 3}]) == 3
    assert apply_patch([1, 2], [{"op": "add", "path": "/-", "value": 3}]) == [1, 2, 3]
    assert apply_patch([1, 2], [{"op": "add", "path": "/2", "value": 3}]) == [1, 2, 3]
    assert apply_patch([1, 2], [{"op": "add", "path": "/0", "value": 0}]) == [0, 1, 2]
    with pytest.raises(PatchError):
        apply_patch([1], [{"op": "add", "path": "/3", "value": 0}])
    with pytest.raises(PatchError):
        apply_patch({}, [{"op": "add", "path": "/a/b", "value": 0}])


def test_remove_replace():
    assert apply_patch({"a": 1}, [{"op": "remove", "path": "/a"}]) == {}
    with pytest.raises(PatchError):
        apply_patch({"a": 1}, [{"op": "remove", "path": "/b"}])
    with pytest.raises(PatchError):
        apply_patch([1], [{"op": "remove", "path": "/1"}])
    with pytest.raises(PatchError):
        apply_patch([1], [{"op": "remove", "path": "/-"}])
    assert apply_patch([1, 2], [{"op": "replace", "path": "/1", "value": 9}]) == [1, 9]
    assert apply_patch({"a": 1}, [{"op": "replace", "path": "", "value": None}]) is None
    with pytest.raises(PatchError):
        apply_patch({}, [{"op": "replace", "path": "/a", "value": 1}])


def test_move_copy():
    assert apply_patch({"a": 1}, [{"op": "move", "path": "/b", "from": "/a"}]) == {"b": 1}
    assert apply_patch([1, 2, 3], [{"op": "move", "path": "/2", "from": "/0"}]) == [2, 3, 1]
    with pytest.raises(PatchError):
        apply_patch({"a": {"b": 1}}, [{"op": "move", "path": "/a/b/c", "from": "/a"}])
    with pytest.raises(PatchError):
        apply_patch({}, [{"op": "move", "path": "/b", "from": "/a"}])
    d = {"a": {"x": [1]}}
    r = apply_patch(d, [{"op": "copy", "path": "/b", "from": "/a"}])
    r["b"]["x"].append(2)
    assert r["a"]["x"] == [1]


def test_test_op():
    ok = lambda v, t: apply_patch({"a": v}, [{"op": "test", "path": "/a", "value": t}])
    ok(1, 1.0)
    ok({"x": [1, 2]}, {"x": [1.0, 2]})
    for v, t in [(True, 1), (1, True), (0, False), ({"x": True}, {"x": 1}), ([1], [1, 2]), (None, 0)]:
        with pytest.raises(PatchError):
            ok(v, t)
    ok(True, True)


def test_atomic_and_in_place():
    d = {"a": [1, 2]}
    orig = copy.deepcopy(d)
    bad = [{"op": "add", "path": "/a/-", "value": 3}, {"op": "remove", "path": "/zz"}]
    for ip in (False, True):
        with pytest.raises(PatchError):
            apply_patch(d, bad, in_place=ip)
        assert d == orig
    good = [{"op": "add", "path": "/a/-", "value": 3}]
    r = apply_patch(d, good)
    assert d == orig and r["a"] == [1, 2, 3]
    r = apply_patch(d, good, in_place=True)
    assert r is d and d["a"] == [1, 2, 3]


def test_input_value_not_aliased():
    v = {"k": []}
    r = apply_patch({}, [{"op": "add", "path": "/a", "value": v}])
    r["a"]["k"].append(1)
    assert v == {"k": []}


@pytest.mark.parametrize("patch", [
    {"op": "add"}, [1], [{"op": "bogus", "path": ""}], [{"op": "add", "path": "/a"}],
    [{"op": "move", "path": "/a"}], [{"op": "add", "path": 1, "value": 1}],
    [{"op": "copy", "path": "/a", "from": 3}], [{"path": "/a"}],
])
def test_malformed(patch):
    with pytest.raises(PatchError):
        apply_patch({"a": 1}, patch)
